original_question: What type of heart arrhythmia, characterized by a resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute, can occur in individuals with Emery–Dreifuss muscular dystrophy?

final_qi.question: What type of heart arrhythmia, characterized by a resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute, can occur in individuals with Emery–Dreifuss muscular dystrophy?
final_qi.search_keyword: heart arrhythmia resting heart rate below 60 Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy
final_qi.long_answer: Bradycardia is a type of heart arrhythmia characterized by a resting heart rate of less than 60 beats per minute. In individuals with Emery–Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, various cardiac conduction abnormalities may occur, leading to a reduced heart rate and other arrhythmias. Bradycardia in this context can be a result of the underlying muscle degeneration and subsequent disturbances in the electrical conduction system of the heart.

Whether or not a given individual's brain can deal effectively with stress, and thus their susceptibility to depression, depends on the β-catenin in each person's brain, according to a study conducted at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and published November 12, 2014, in the journal Nature.[73] Higher β-catenin signaling increases behavioral flexibility, whereas defective β-catenin signaling leads to depression and reduced stress management.[73] Altered expression profiles in β-catenin have been associated with dilated cardiomyopathy in humans. β-Catenin upregulation of expression has generally been observed in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.[74] In a particular study, patients with end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy showed almost doubled estrogen receptor alpha (ER-alpha) mRNA and protein levels, and the ER-alpha/beta-catenin interaction, present at intercalated discs of control, non-diseased human hearts was lost, suggesting that the loss of this interaction at the intercalated disc may play a role in the progression of heart failure.[75] Together with BCL9 and PYGO proteins, β-catenin coordinates different aspects of heard development, and mutations in Bcl9 or Pygo in model organisms - such as the mouse and zebrafish - cause phenotypes that are very similar to human congenital heart disorders.[76] β-Catenin is a proto-oncogene. Mutations of this gene are commonly found in a variety of cancers: in primary hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, ovarian carcinoma, breast cancer, lung cancer and glioblastoma. It has been estimated that approximately 10% of all tissue samples sequenced from all cancers display mutations in the CTNNB1 gene.[77] Most of these mutations cluster on a tiny area of the N-terminal segment of β-catenin: the β-TrCP binding motif. Loss-of-function mutations of this motif essentially make ubiquitinylation and degradation of β-catenin impossible. It will cause β-catenin to translocate to the nucleus without any external stimulus and continuously drive transcription of its target genes. Increased nuclear β-catenin levels have also been noted in basal cell carcinoma (BCC),[78] head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), prostate cancer (CaP),[79] pilomatrixoma (PTR)[80] and medulloblastoma (MDB)[81] These observations may or may not implicate a mutation in the β-catenin gene: other Wnt pathway components can also be faulty.
